title: A locally quasi-finite morphism is locally of finite type (Stacks, remark after 01TD)
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]: every $x\in X$ has an affine open neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}A=U\subseteq X$ and an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R=V\subseteq S$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$ such that $R\to A$ is of finite type and quasi-finite at the prime of $A$ corresponding to $x$. Then $f$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

source.place: Morphisms, Section Tag 01TC (section-quasi-finite), remark after Definition Tag 01TD, line 3558 ('Trivially, a locally quasi-finite morphism is locally of finite type'); the locality of finite type it rests on is Lemma Tag 01T2 (lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize), line 2673
